guardedDialogs.humanAction: Answer Codex's folder-trust prompt in the pane. TangleClaw does not accept folder trust on your behalf.

evidence.source: Live captures of codex-cli 0.156.1 launched as `codex --no-daemon` in a folder its home did not trust (throwaway CODEX_HOME, private tmux server). The dialog reads `Trust this folder? Codex can read, edit, and run files here…`, with `› 1. Trust and continue` highlighted and `enter continue · esc quit` below. It was first drawn between 2.7 s and 3.8 s after the pane was created, below the opening composer row, which stays on screen above it.

guardedDialogs.humanAction: Answer Codex's update prompt in the pane (Escape skips it). TangleClaw does not answer it: its default is to upgrade the global Codex install.

evidence.source: Live captures of codex-cli 0.156.1 with update checks at Codex's default and a home that had already learned of 0.161.0. The dialog reads `Update available · 0.156.1 → 0.161.0`, with `› 1. Update now (runs `npm install -g @openai/codex`)` highlighted and `enter continue · esc skip` below. First drawn between 0.4 s and 3.7 s after the pane was created, before the folder-trust prompt. An `Enter` sent to it in a sandbox ran the install and ended the pane (#2177). After it is skipped its rows stay in scrollback above the live composer, and a notice box reads `Update available!` without the middle dot, which this pattern does not match.

fullAuto.label: Full Auto
fullAuto.description: Never asks for approval, still sandboxed to the workspace
fullAuto.warning: Sandboxed but unattended — review the generated diffs before merging.

bypassPermissions.label: Bypass
bypassPermissions.description: Skips every approval AND the sandbox (containers/VMs only)

flag.source: codex-cli 0.156.1 `--help` lists `-m, --model <MODEL>`. Measured on the product's own launch shape, a `--remote` client of a per-launch app-server started by this adapter: with the account's configured default at gpt-6-sol, `codex --remote unix://<socket> --model 'gpt-5.6-sol'` produced a thread whose `thread/read` model is gpt-5.6-sol, and the same with gpt-6-luna. The flag is not ignored on a remote client.

offered.source: One short turn on each id on this account, started over the protocol on the thread the pane opened: both completed (5 s and 8 s) and each rollout's `turn_context` names the requested model. This is evidence for this account on this date, which is why the roster is read again at every save and launch instead of trusting this list.

roster.source: `~/.codex/models_cache.json` (or `$CODEX_HOME`): `models[].slug` and `display_name`, with `fetched_at` rewritten when the CLI starts (observed moving from 21:25Z to 21:52Z across two launches the same day). It also lists entries with `visibility: hide` (gpt-reserve, codex-auto-review), which is why the offered list is an allowlist and not the roster. `maxAgeHours` of 168 is a judgment, not a measurement: long enough that a machine used weekly still validates, short enough that a list from a CLI nobody has started in a month is not called current.

evidence.source: Signed-in codex-cli 0.161.0 over the launch path TangleClaw uses (a `codex app-server` per launch, the pane's TUI attached with `--remote`), throwaway CODEX_HOME, private tmux server, whole pane and cursor read together, 2026-10-12. At rest the composer has two rows below it: the status row, then exactly `  ? for shortcuts`, on the default status line, a three-item one and a single-item one, after a turn, after a skipped update prompt and after a resume. The screen it opens with, and the `Resuming session…` screen, draw that footer ALONE under an empty composer with the cursor on it (first seen 387 to 413 ms after launch over six launches, and at 427 ms on a resume, where the thread read idle at 625 to 634 ms while that screen was still up). No header row names a model. A plain `codex` launch on the shared daemon draws a different footer (`  ← for agents · ? for shortcuts`, captured 2026-10-07) and is not this launch path. While an answer streams, codex-cli 0.161.0 draws no busy row: the composer is empty with the cursor on it and these two rows are below it, as at rest (one real turn, 2026-10-12, read while the thread reported `active`). Not inferred from any other version.

Signed-in codex-cli 0.162.0 over the launch path TangleClaw uses (a `codex app-server` per launch, the pane's TUI attached with `--remote`), throwaway CODEX_HOME, private tmux server, whole pane and cursor read together, 2026-10-12. At rest the composer has two rows below it: the status row, then exactly `  ? for shortcuts`, on the default status line, a three-item one and a single-item one, after a turn, after a skipped update prompt and after a resume. The screen it opens with, and the `Resuming session…` screen, draw that footer ALONE under an empty composer with the cursor on it (first seen 702 to 1137 ms after launch over five launches, at 516 ms on a resume, and at 407 ms under an empty status line). No header row names a model. As typing began, one frame drew the status row with the footer absent. While an answer streams, codex-cli 0.162.0 draws no busy row: the composer is empty with the cursor on it and these two rows are below it, as at rest (one real turn, 2026-10-12, read while the thread reported `active`). Not inferred from any other version.

busyMarker.source: Live capture of a working codex pane (codex-cli 0.154.0, gpt-6-astra): the status row renders `• Working (23s • esc to interrupt)`. `esc to interrupt` is the stable half of that line; the elapsed seconds change every tick. NOT sufficient alone here — codex keeps its composer drawn mid-turn, which is why `idleMarker` is also set. Key bindings are user-configurable, so a rebound interrupt key would change this string; that is a known limit of every marker in this block, not a defect of this one.

promptPattern.source: Live capture. An EMPTY codex composer is not a bare glyph — it draws the glyph, a separator, then the dim placeholder `Ask Codex to do anything`. Matching the placeholder is a POSITIVE test for a bare prompt: typing replaces it, so a half-typed line stops matching, and a dialog row (`› 1. Yes, continue`, seen on the directory-trust prompt) never matches. Two things were measured rather than assumed. The line cannot be end-anchored: codex draws an animated braille shimmer across it, so it rarely ends at the placeholder. And the separator cell is not reliably a space — the shimmer OVERWRITES it, observed live as `›⠁Ask Codex to do anything⡁`, so the class accepts a space, an NBSP, or one braille cell (U+2800-U+28FF). A pattern requiring a space there matched 0 of 1 live captures and was corrected.

promptGlyph.source: Live capture: U+203A SINGLE RIGHT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK, rendered bold (`\x1b[1m›\x1b[0m`), at column 0 of the composer line. Observed identical across gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-6-astra at low/medium/high reasoning effort. Not established as invariant across themes or future versions.

promptPad.source: Live capture: one ordinary space (U+0020) between glyph and first input column, not an NBSP as Claude uses. Confirmed by cursor position — tmux reports cursor_x=2 with the glyph at column 0 on an empty composer, across 12 samples.

placeholderSgr.source: Live capture: the placeholder is emitted as `\u001b[2mAsk Codex to do anything`, i.e. SGR 2 (dim), the same attribute Claude uses. The braille shimmer is NOT outside this field merely because it carries only a truecolor foreground. `_cells` applies SGR sub-parameters as attributes, so `\u001b[38;2;R;G;Bm` records 38, 2 and R — the 2 from the truecolor selector is indistinguishable from a real dim attribute, and a probe confirms `sgr.has(2)` is true for such a cell. The shimmer is therefore handled by `decorativePattern`, which names it explicitly, rather than by this field happening to catch it.

idleMarker.source: Measured from outside the pane over 50 samples at 1.5s intervals against a live codex session: the status row reads `· Ready ·` at rest and `· Working ·` during a turn — present in 45/45 at-rest samples, absent in 5/5 working samples, zero overlap. Required because codex keeps its composer drawn during a turn, so the composer-empty read alone would call a working pane idle. The separators are part of the declared marker on purpose: the gate matches with `includes()` over the whole captured tail, so a bare `Ready` would also be satisfied by ordinary transcript text such as a tool line reading `Ready in 1.2s`, which is not an at-rest signal at all. `· Ready ·` is the status row's own rendering and was confirmed present on the live pane. Known limit, NOT measured: a cold pane that has not yet drawn its status row has no idle marker, and declaring one puts codex on the readiness-gated prime paste (`lib/sessions.js#_awaitPaneReady`). Every sample here was taken on a warm session; a freshly launched codex pane did render the status row with `Ready` in it during startup captures, but the gate's cold-start timing was not measured.

decorativePattern.source: Measured, not predicted. codex paints an animated braille shimmer (U+2800-U+28FF) across the composer line AND the lines above it, continuously, in any session that has conversation history. It broke both idle gates. Movement: `_paneDigest` hashes the transcript region above the composer, where part of the shimmer is drawn — 8 distinct digests over 8 samples of a completely idle pane, so the monitor reported `pane-writing` forever and the nudge could never fire. Composer: a shimmer cell lands between glyph and cursor about a third of the time (8 empty / 4 blocked, reproduced in two independent 12-sample runs), and it OVERWRITES the pad cell, which made the separator unrecognisable. Declaring the range makes both gates discount cells the ENGINE drew rather than the operator; the digest blanks them to spaces rather than deleting them, so a moving shimmer cannot shorten a line and reintroduce the instability. After the fix, on the same live pane: 1 distinct digest over 8 idle samples, composer 12/12 empty, and the wake nudge fired end to end. Scoped to the engine that draws them — claude and antigravity declare nothing, so braille typed into those engines is still input. Accepted cost, stated rather than hidden: braille an operator genuinely types into codex is discounted as decoration. NOT caused by tui.animations, the model, or reasoning effort — a fresh gpt-6-astra high session with animations ON showed zero shimmer over 12 samples, so it tracks session history rather than configuration.

headerPattern.source: Live captures of codex-cli 0.156.1 (2026-10-07 and 2026-10-11, pane 100x30). That version opens with a header box whose rows read `model:     loading   /model to change` and `directory: <cwd>`; once its thread has started the model row names the model (`model:     GPT-6-Astra   /model to change`). The pattern matches the model row in either state and no other row of the box. The run of spaces after the colon varies with the box's width, which is why this is a pattern. Known limit, measured: codex-cli 0.159.0 and 0.161.0 draw NO such row on any captured screen (their header is `>_ OpenAI Codex (v…)` and the folder), so on those versions nothing matches and this declares nothing about them.

startingPattern.source: Live captures of codex-cli 0.156.1. The model row reads `loading` on the screen Codex opens with, where it already draws an empty composer, and on the folder-trust and update dialogs drawn before a thread exists: every opening screen and startup dialog of 40 runs on 2026-10-07 (28 in the TangleClaw launch shape, 12 in the legacy shape), and the whole dialog reads of 2026-10-11. With a fake API key the row still changed to the model's name when the thread started, so it follows the session and not the account. Read on the NEWEST matching row only: on the main screen the superseded `loading` box stays in the history above the box that names the model. Not established for any version but 0.156.1; see `headerPattern` for the two versions that draw no such row.

restRows.source: Each version's entry carries its own measurement; see `restRows.<version>.evidence`. With an EMPTY status line (`tui.status_line = []`) both versions draw one row at rest, the footer with `100% context left` at its right, which is not the declared footer: the launch gate refuses it and the operator's Fire is needed. While a turn streams its answer, both versions draw no busy row: an empty composer, the status row and the footer, as at rest; the thread's own status is what says a turn is running.

startupControl.channel: One `codex app-server` per launch on a local unix socket, started detached and owned by TangleClaw; the pane's TUI attaches with `--remote` ahead of its launch-mode flags. Fire is `turn/start` on the pane's thread.
startupControl.readiness: Read from the protocol only: the server's version equals the installed and the recorded one; `config/read` trusts the project directory, or holds no trust entry for it while a measured version and a pane witness allow the fire (see `remoteTrustPrompt`); `account/read` names an account; `account/rateLimits/read` explicitly allows usage or reports usable credits; exactly one loaded thread (the recorded one once seen) whose canonical cwd is the project; and it is `idle`. Any unknown answer fails closed.
startupControl.receipt: `clientUserMessageId` echoed as the user item's `clientId` WITH content whose bytes hash to the prompt's text digest is accepted (from `item/completed` or a `thread/turns/list` read-back, re-read on an interval); `turn/completed {completed}` on that turn, after acceptance, is applied; `failed` and `interrupted` are named.
startupControl.blockers: Pre-send: no trust entry in Codex's config for the directory, where the fire is not allowed without one, or an entry there that says anything other than trusted, which never gets the allowance (`trust_required`, worded as what was read, never as a dialog nobody looked for); where the fire is allowed without an entry, a pane not seen at an empty composer (`pane_not_ready`, naming what was seen; a trust dialog actually on the pane is `trust_required`); no account (`auth_required`), exhausted usage with no usable credits (`quota_exhausted`), version disagreement (`version_mismatch`), no single idle thread (`engine_not_ready`), an unreadable answer (`readiness_unknown`). In-turn: `waitingOnApproval` and `waitingOnUserInput` keep the fire accepted under `approval_pending` / `user_input_pending`; the operator answers in the pane.

adapter.source: The startupControl spike (2026-09-23, codex-cli 0.156.1) and the six Chunk B2 probes (2026-09-24), recorded in the #1825 plan. The protocol is WebSocket JSON-RPC (no `jsonrpc` field) on the unix socket; every call named here completed live.

channel.source: Probes 1-6: `--listen unix://<long path>` binds a short path under /private/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>/ and leaves a symlink; the TUI needs the short path (SUN_LEN). `-a never -s workspace-write` after `--remote` reached the thread (status line `never`; `thread/start` echoes the policy). SIGTERM exits 0 and removes the socket.

readiness.source: Probes 1-6: `initialize.userAgent` carries the server version; `config/read` returns `config.projects[path].trust_level`; an untrusted cwd leaves the TUI at its trust dialog with NO loaded thread; `thread/read` reports `status.type` idle; `account/read` and `account/rateLimits/read` answered as recorded in the plan. A fresh thread cannot be resumed or listed before its first user message, so subscription is not a readiness precondition. Corrected 2026-10-07 (#2186): the statement that an untrusted cwd leaves the TUI at its trust dialog was not reproduced. Under `--remote` on codex-cli 0.156.1 no trust dialog was drawn in 11 of 11 private fake-key launches of an untrusted folder, nor in one live signed-in launch into a renamed directory; the pane reached its ordinary composer with an idle thread. A home that has never trusted a folder answers `config.projects: null`. Measured 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12 (#2059), signed-in codex-cli 0.156.1 under `--remote` on a scratch server, a throwaway CODEX_HOME holding a copy of the sign-in, Codex's default status line (`GPT-6-Astra default · <cwd>`, no `Ready` item): gated on the status-line marker, the launch's automatic fire was never sent and the row read `blocked (pane_not_ready)` after 90 s; gated on the launch's idle thread and the pane witness, it was `applied` with no hand Fire, about 9 s after launch, in a trusted folder and in a folder with no trust entry. A launch that met the update prompt had no loaded thread while the dialog was up and was held for the whole window with nothing typed; a hand Fire after Escape was then applied. Not measured: a resumed session, and a custom status line under a live automatic fire (its pane was captured and is judged by the witness in tests).

receipt.source: Spike case 3 (2026-09-23, three benign turns): `turn/start` with `clientUserMessageId` produced `item/completed {type: userMessage, clientId: <ours>}` then `turn/completed {status: completed}`. B2 live check (2026-09-24, one operator-authorized turn, the real adapter): `thread/resume` on the freshly materialized thread was refused (`list_turns is not supported yet`), the `thread/turns/list` read-back carried the echoed clientId with the prompt's exact text (accepted 0.25 s after the send), and `turn/completed {completed}` followed (applied); the pane rendered the prompt as a user turn. The watcher therefore also re-reads the record on an interval rather than relying on a subscription.

blockers.source: Spike case 4 and probes 1, 5: `account/rateLimits/read` names an exhausted window and credits; an untrusted cwd shows the TUI's trust dialog while `thread/start` from the protocol succeeds, so trust is checked through `config/read` before a send; `thread/status/changed {active, activeFlags: [waitingOnApproval]}` plus a server request name an in-turn approval, and the operator's decline ends the turn `interrupted`. Corrected 2026-10-07 (#2186): `trust_required` is read from `config/read` alone and no longer asserts a dialog; the pane is read only by the fire's pane witness.

verifiedVersions.source: codex-cli 0.156.1 is the only version the spike and the probes ran against; the protocol is marked [experimental] by the CLI, so no other version is assumed. codex-cli 0.161.0 and 0.162.0 were each measured signed in on 2026-10-12, each in its own run on a scratch TangleClaw whose own copy of this profile listed that one version (#2059): the launch's automatic fire applied on the default and on a three-item status line, a folder with no trust entry was refused, the update prompt was held and named, and the wake held on the thread's `active` answer on every tick of a real streaming turn. NEITHER IS LISTED, because of one further run on each: with the pane's TUI process stopped mid-answer and the turn then ending, the thread read idle under a pane still showing the answer being written, the wake read that pane as at the prompt and typed its nudge into it (0.161.0: about 16 s after the thread read idle and 38 s before the pane was redrawn; 0.162.0: about 16 s and 37 s). On these versions a streaming answer is drawn exactly like a session at rest, so the pane cannot contradict a late idle answer. The still frame was made by stopping the renderer, not by a pause in the model. Listing either needs a gate that positively refuses a pane not redrawn since the turn ended, proved for that version.

remoteTrustPrompt.source: codex-cli 0.156.1 is listed on one signed-in probe sitting (2026-10-11, #2186, Architect A154's gate): a scratch TangleClaw on the activating branch, a private tmux server, a Codex home holding a signed-in account and no trust entry, and the operator's Fire through the real `--remote` path, in two new folders. Folder one, plain: the pane reached the ordinary composer and drew no trust dialog; with this list empty the Fire was refused `trust_required` and nothing was sent; with 0.156.1 listed the Fire was accepted and applied, the turn rendered and was answered, the row carried the dispatch note, and Codex's `config.toml` held no `[projects]` entry afterwards. Folder two, holding its own `.codex/config.toml` and hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit): a Fire while Codex's update prompt was on screen was refused `engine_not_ready`; once the prompt was skipped the Fire was accepted and applied with the note; no hook ran and the folder's config was not applied, and Codex's own startup warning says project-local config, hooks and exec policies are disabled until the project is trusted, while skills still load. The witness accepted that pane's status row, which carried Codex's `1 warning · f2 to view` item. Not measured signed-in: the automatic launch fire. On a Codex home with the default status line the launch's own pane gate never saw its at-rest marker and recorded `pane_not_ready` before this allowance was reached, so both sends were the operator's Fire. Earlier, for the same version and launch path: 11 private launches with a fake API key (git and non-git folders, a fresh home, a home with other trusted projects, default and Full Auto modes, and after a skipped update prompt) and one live signed-in launch into a renamed directory (2026-10-07); in all twelve no trust dialog was drawn. This is a measurement of one version. A version in this list never permits a send by itself: the fire's pane witness must still see an empty composer at fire time.
